findings.description: Critical: Round-1 B1 rewrote Profile-Aware Setup so the entrypoint owns precondition checking, but three of its scenarios still have no task, no red-phase test, and no work-packages gate. Mapped all 27 `#### Scenario:` headings in specs/setup-coordinator/spec.md against every quoted scenario name in tasks.md: 'Local profile setup' (spec.md:16-25), 'Railway profile setup' (spec.md:27-34), and 'Secrets file missing' (spec.md:36-41) are UNREFERENCED. Task 3.6 is the only `check` implementation task and lists only 'Agents file resolved from configuration' (tasks.md:158-163); rg over tasks.md for secret/docker/ParadeDB/container/Railway/Local returns zero hits. So the four local preconditions (runtime, ParadeDB health, MCP registration, tool discovery), the five Railway steps (URL resolve, curl /health, write-endpoint auth, coordination_bridge detect, capability flags), and the missing-.secrets.yaml report path have no scheduled work. Scenario clause 4 ('coordination tools discoverable through the registered MCP server') also has no probe design that stays inside the no-agent-coordinator-import rule.
findings.resolution: Add a Phase-3 red-phase test task and extend task 3.6's Spec scenarios to name Local profile setup, Railway profile setup, and Secrets file missing. Specify how each local precondition is observed (e.g. shutil.which for docker/podman; docker inspect/compose ps for ParadeDB; parse vendor MCP config files for registration) without importing agent-coordinator. For clause 4, either define a portable discovery check or drop it from the scenario. Assert Secrets reports the exact copy command and does not create the file.

findings.description: Critical: Round-1 B2 made degraded runs expressible (`degraded`/`warnings` required at harness-report.schema.json:8; scenarios at spec.md:90-99) but left them unenforced, so the fail-open can still ship. Neither 'Degraded run is distinguishable from an empty one' nor 'Complete run asserts completeness' is named by any task; task 1.4 says only 'same as 1.3, 1.3a, 1.3b' (tasks.md:60). The wp-core contract gate (work-packages.yaml:146-148) runs one successful detect-harnesses and accepts `degraded:false`/`warnings:[]`, so an implementation that hardcodes those two values passes every declared gate. New inconsistency introduced by the fix: schema.md description and the Degraded scenario list 'unreadable roster' as a degraded-report cause, while task 1.3a / Agents-file scenario require an unresolvable roster to exit non-zero before producing a report — so the named degradation source cannot appear in JSON under the current task graph.
findings.resolution: Add a Phase-1 red-phase task covering both degradation scenarios: force sibling ImportError (vendor_health/yaml) and/or a skipped layer, assert degraded=true with a non-empty warnings entry, and assert a clean run has degraded=false and warnings=[]. Name both scenarios on task 1.4. Reconcile 'unreadable roster': either emit --json with degraded=true and non-zero exit, or remove 'unreadable roster' from the degraded scenario/schema description and keep resolve-miss as exit-nonzero-only. Add a wp-core verification step that forces a degraded run and asserts degraded is true so the flag cannot be a constant.

findings.description: Critical: Round-1 B3 added scenario 'Fallback write is atomic' (spec.md:179-182) and design.md:139-143 requires the inline fallback to do tmp→fsync→os.replace, but no task forces or asserts the fallback path. Task 2.3 names 'Sibling skill unavailable', 'Concurrent reader safety', and 'Settings file is not in canonical JSON form' (tasks.md:114-115), not 'Fallback write is atomic'. Task 2.1 parametrizes only {legacy_shim, new writer} (tasks.md:91-94) — the legacy-vs-new axis — so the import-failure branch is dead under test. Verified the hazard is real: provenance.py:55-61 still ends in `target.write_bytes(payload)`. Copying that body would reintroduce defect #3 while every declared gate stays green because project-context-runtime is present in this repo.
findings.resolution: Extend task 2.1 with a second axis {imported atomic_write_bytes, inline fallback} by monkeypatching the import to raise ImportError; on the fallback leg assert the write goes through a temp path + os.replace (no partial content) and unrelated keys stay byte-identical. Name 'Fallback write is atomic' in task 2.3's Spec scenarios line.

findings.description: Critical: Script-Backed Entrypoint requires binary exit codes '0 when the requested state is satisfied, non-zero when it is not' (spec.md:64) but never defines satisfied for detect-harnesses (or report). Presence reporting can succeed while vendors are cli_missing/unknown — the live roster has antigravity-local (no artifact → unknown) and pi-local (needs OPENROUTER_API_KEY). Task 3.1 covers 'exit-code discipline' without pinning mixed-state reports to 0 or non-zero. The wp-core contract gate (work-packages.yaml:148) does `sys.exit(...) if r.returncode else None` before schema validation, so an implementation that treats 'all ready' as the satisfied state makes the gate fail on ordinary developer hosts for the wrong reason; an implementation that always exits 0 on a completed report also conforms. Two plan-following implementations diverge and one breaks the declared verification step.
findings.resolution: Add an explicit SHALL: detect-harnesses exits 0 when a roster was resolved and a report emitted (presence check succeeded), independent of per-vendor state; reserve non-zero for resolve failures, usage errors, and (if retained) hard degradation modes. State the analogous satisfied-state rule for check/configure/report. Pin the rule in task 3.1's tests.

findings.description: Nit: Round-1 B4 added `cli_on_path: {"const": true}` to the unknown branch (harness-report.schema.json:127-135), but scenario 'Vendor has no detectable config location' (spec.md:116-120) is still unconditional — WHEN a vendor declares no artifact, THEN state=unknown, with no CLI-present precondition. Design D5 and task 1.4 fix precedence as cli_missing → unknown → ready/config_missing (design.md:200-202; tasks.md:59). Verified with Draft202012Validator: a VendorReport with state=unknown and cli_on_path=false yields exactly one error (`True was expected`). Task 1.3 owns this scenario and can build a fixture with neither CLI nor artifact, then assert the state the scenario literally promises — producing a schema-invalid document or a test that disagrees with D5.
findings.resolution: Update the scenario WHEN clause to 'WHEN a vendor's CLI is on PATH and it declares no home-directory configuration artifact to check', aligning spec, D5 precedence, and the schema conditional.

findings.description: Nit: The B3 edit left a requirement-level SHALL stranded inside a scenario block. spec.md:183 — 'Where a sibling module depends on a third-party package that a consumer payload may not provide, the resulting failure SHALL be caught at the point of use and reported as a degraded capability' — belongs in the Portable Skill Payload bullet list (spec.md:173-177). It currently sits after the THEN/AND bullets of 'Fallback write is atomic', reading as a third assertion of that scenario despite being about pyyaml-style third-party degradation (design.md:311 Risks). openspec validate --strict does not catch this.
findings.resolution: Move the spec.md:183 bullet into the requirement bullet list immediately after spec.md:177; leave the Fallback write is atomic scenario with only its WHEN/THEN/AND clauses.

findings.description: Nit: contracts/README.md:51-58 delegates summary cardinality to the test suite ('summary.total must equal len(vendors)'; each counter equals the count of vendors in that state) because JSON Schema cannot express it, but no task creates that assertion. Task 1.3 covers four states / unknown / validity disclaimer and never mentions summary. Confirmed: a document with vendors:[] and summary.total:99 validates with 0 errors against harness-report.schema.json. The sibling delegation in the same paragraph ('at most one entry per vendor key') IS covered by task 1.3b, which makes this look like an oversight.
findings.resolution: Add a summary-consistency assertion to task 1.3: recompute the five counters from the emitted vendors array and assert equality with summary.*.

findings.description: Nit: The sub-decision table in proposal.md is split by an inserted refinement paragraph, so D3/D4 render as orphaned rows. The table opens at proposal.md:150 with header + D1/D2, then lines 155-167 insert prose about D1a/D1b/D2, then lines 168-169 resume bare `| D3 |` / `| D4 |` rows with no header. Markdown will not render those rows as part of the original table, even though line 148 promises four sub-decisions fixed at the same gate.
findings.resolution: Move the D1a/D1b/D2 refinement paragraph (proposal.md:155-167) below the full D1–D4 table so all four rows stay contiguous under one header.

findings.description: Optional: Scenario 'Tests do not touch operator state' (spec.md:212-215) is the seventh UNREFERENCED scenario in the systematic map. Behavior is partially covered by task notes (tmp_path / fake HOME) and manual checklist V.6 (tasks.md:243-244), but no task's Spec scenarios line names it and no automated assertion prevents a future test from reading real `~` or the repo settings file. Lower risk than the B1–B3 gaps because implementers are repeatedly warned, but the scenario-to-task map is still incomplete.
findings.resolution: Either name the scenario on tasks 1.3/2.1 (and optionally add a suite-level guard that fails if HOME is the real home or if .claude/settings.local.json is opened) or fold the scenario into V.6-only and drop it from the ADDED requirement if it is not meant to be a testable Spec scenario.

findings.description: Verified positives that should survive the next iterate: (1) harness-report.schema.json conditionals bite — ready+null artifact, ready+empty artifact, unknown+cli_on_path:false, degraded+empty warnings each produce errors under Draft202012Validator; (2) design file:line claims hold — vendor_health D6 at :99-101, load_agents_yaml :110-155 with exists()-guarded explicit path then network then cwd then {}, check_vendor defaults command to "", atomic canonical_json_bytes sort_keys=True, provenance.py fallback is write_bytes, SKILL.md:211-232 has all four defects, frontmatter omits user_invocable so D9 tail-block obligation is real, cross_skill_dependencies.setup-coordinator is currently [coordination-bridge] at install-manifest.json top level; (3) verification commands are executable as written — install.sh --check works, validate_install_manifest and dependency_direction both require --skills-root, skills/.venv has jsonschema+pyyaml while system python3 does not; (4) wp-core/wp-integration write_allow overlap on test_skill_md.py is sound because depends_on: [wp-core] makes the packages sequential.
findings.resolution: Keep these constraints and gates; do not regress them while fixing findings 1–4.
